subtitle: Gain Utility
tagline: One level control in decibels or perceived-loudness percent, with smoothed changes and a safety limiter at −0.1 dBFS.

body.lead: TB Volume is a one-control gain utility. Drag the large numeric value to set the level, and choose whether it reads in decibels or in a perceived-loudness percentage.

body.p: dB mode covers −24 to +24 dB. Percent mode uses a Sone-based scale from silence (0%) to 300%, where 100% is unity and 200% aims to sound about twice as loud. Level changes are smoothed to avoid clicks, and a stereo-linked sample-peak limiter keeps the output at or below −0.1 dBFS.

ul: One `OUTPUT LEVEL` value: drag up to increase, down to decrease
dB mode (−24 to +24 dB) or Sone-based percent mode (0 to 300%)
20 ms gain smoothing for click-free changes and automation
Built-in stereo-linked limiter at −0.1 dBFS with 1 ms lookahead

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Volume 1.2.2 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.0.8 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Volume where you need a level change. It starts at unity: 0.0 dB.
Drag the `OUTPUT LEVEL` value up to make the signal louder or down to make it quieter.
Automate the level if needed; changes are smoothed over 20 ms.

rows: Previous and next preset, the preset list (Init or a saved user preset; CUSTOM after a change), and Save.
The level value. Drag vertically to change it.
Sets the gain. Drag up to increase volume or down to decrease it. Changes are smoothed over 20 ms.
dB uses the −24 to +24 dB scale. % uses the 0 to 300 percent Sone-based scale, where 100% is unity and 0% is silence.

note.text: Both modes drive the same Normalized Level parameter, and both read unity at the default value. Away from unity the two scales are mapped differently, so listen again after switching mode.

body.p: After the gain, a stereo-linked sample-peak limiter with 1 ms of lookahead keeps the output at or below −0.1 dBFS. It is always on and has no controls. Because of the lookahead, TB Volume always has about 1 ms of latency, which the host compensates.

warn.text: The limiter catches sample peaks, not true peaks. It is a safety net, not a mastering limiter. For deliveries with a true-peak limit, use a true-peak limiter at the end of the chain.

body.p: Use the arrows to step through presets, or open the list to choose Init or a saved user preset. Save stores the current settings as a .tbvolumepreset file. The name shows CUSTOM after you change a setting.
